title: [CQ-R13] Isolation integration and hardening
description:
Objective: Certify provisioning, ownership, malicious writer/test containment, cancellation and recovery on supported hardware.

Deliverable: Isolation integration and hardening. This is task R13 of the approved full CQ rollout; consume this contract, not the whole reference document.

Scope boundaries: implement this behavior and its regression tests only. Later activation, other platform/client consumers and other task behaviors remain out of scope unless named here. Approved full CQ-01–CQ-08 rollout from the interactive implementation plan (2026-10-24). CQ-01 is already landed. Use original Moe source; daemon owns state, wrappers own host Git writes. User selected Moe-provisioned LOCAL Linux VMs (not cloud CI), coding/QA and checks isolated, and exact designated LOCAL BRANCH delivery. Strong profile stays disabled until isolation, evidence and client gates pass. Preserve legacy behavior and existing dirty bytes. Never directly edit .moe. No second revision authority, scheduler, graph database or native memory database.

Verification command (fresh, exit0 required): node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs

Dependency aliases (wired by Moe task ids after import): R03, R04, R05, R10, R11, R12.
definitionOfDone: Real Windows/Linux/macOS provisioning evidence establishes each support claim.
Unsupported certification remains blocked without silent fallback.
Fresh verification `node --test scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs` exits0 and its output is supplied to complete_task.
taskRails: No direct .moe edits; no Git-write commands by agents; wrappers own landing.
Do not enable verified-local or claim isolation until all requisite implementation and certification gates pass.

implementationPlan.note:
Adversarial review of the CQ-R epic diff: four review agents plus my own pass. I verified each finding below against the code; probes ran only under /tmp.

IN-SCOPE FIXES (tests watched fail, then pass):
A. runCheckJob copied the caller's provider without the platform's pinned client, and landedRunCheck passes none. So every call after provisioning (materialize, toolchain and deps install, session, verify, delete) ran a bare `multipass`. parse() now pins `provider.executable ?? platform.executable` (check-lifecycle.mjs). Test: RX6.
B. The certify cancellation check reported NOT_STARTED or TIMED_OUT ahead of a failed VM delete, against CERTIFICATION.md. It now reports VM_NOT_DELETED first, as containment and canary do (certify-lifecycle.mjs). Test: LC2, three new rows.
D. Dependency install. npm 11.19 (the pinned toolchain's npm) installs candidate bytes three ways:
- it prefers an npm-shrinkwrap.json to the approved lockfile;
- an .npmrc with dry-run=true keeps a committed node_modules;
- it adopts a parent package.json or workspace root, with that parent's lockfile.
Confirmed in the npm 11.19.0 source, plus probes. install_dependencies now requires a regular package.json and refuses an npm-shrinkwrap.json or .npmrc (exit 81, before any install). OFFLINE_INSTALL_ARGS gains --workspaces=false, in the JS list and its Python mirror. Tests: KI3 (three rows), DC4. DC5 passes against the real host npm.
The out-of-plan paths are recorded with declare_files, since there is no amend_plan_step tool.

comments.author: architect-26ba32c3
comments.content:
Architect note from planning CQ-R01 (task-3b760109…, plan rev 1): these strong-profile hardening items were deliberately deferred to this integration task.

R01 ships IDE-session-scoped protection only. Its design (Serena mem: decision-protected-runtime-selection):
- strict fail-closed profile read;
- a JVM-session downgrade pin;
- installed-only daemon, wrapper and proxy selection;
- spawn-record provenance (pid + startInstant, or the direct parent) checked in doConnect.

Follow-ups for R13:
1. **Persistent provenance across IDE restarts.** Today an already-running daemon after an IDE restart is refused by design. Records need storage outside the repo (IDE system dir).
2. **Persistent downgrade pin plus a confirmation UI.** A repo edit of project.json → legacy should need explicit human confirmation across restarts, not only within one session.
3. **Auto-stop or replace of an unverified daemon** via the installed CLI's `stop`, taking care with daemons VS Code shares.
4. **Windows restartDaemon race.** Process.destroy is TerminateProcess, which orphans `_run`, and an old supervisor can respawn it after Restart Daemon.
5. **daemon.json port↔pid binding.** It is not portably verifiable; decide whether same-user host processes stay out of the threat model.
6. **Wrapper-side fallbacks under strong.** Both moe-agent wrappers fall back to their own root, then the global install, when MOE_PROXY_PATH/MOE_DAEMON_PATH vanish.
7. **VS Code parity** for the same selection and provenance rules.

agentCommand/CUSTOM and WSL/native sessions under strong are R10's.

comments.author: qa-952969be
comments.content:
QA follow-up from CQ-R11c (task-53daa94f, approved at 2f2b5e48). It does not block that task, so it goes here for the hardening pass.

In scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs, C5's row 'close before EOF' emits proc.emit('close', 0, null) synchronously, before the PassThrough delivers HELLO and OBS. That row is infra-failure through !s.opened, so check-session.mjs outcomeOf's `|| !s.ended` guard is never pinned: a mutant that drops it survives `^C[1-7] `. The guard itself works, as a QA probe shows: frames parsed, then close 0 with stdout open, gives infra-failure.

Fix: defer the close, e.g. `setImmediate(() => proc.emit('close', 0, null))`. It changes one line and still kills the stop-after-settle mutant the row was added for.

Details are in comment-997358d583ff4f2b9c0f9c779df7172f on task-53daa94f.

comments.author: architect-4ae016fb
comments.content:
Docs-sweep item from CQ-R11e rev 2 (task-001d8ab3, plan revision 2). I kept it out of that row because docs/MCP_SERVER.md is planned by four WORKING rows.

The local runner's check dispatch (scripts/local-runner/check-dispatch.mjs) now decides a required check's offline npm dependency phase from its approved definition.
- Each `configs` entry that is exactly `package-lock.json`, or ends in `/package-lock.json`, adds that dir: '.' for the root.
- A configs directory root never adds one, and no other lockfile in the candidate is installed.
- A definition naming no lockfile gets no dependency phase.
- An owed quality gate with no required check of the same command stops the dispatch before any VM with RUNNER_DEPENDENCIES_UNDECLARED. The fix is to declare the gate's command as a required check, listing its lockfiles or none.

Please document this in docs/MCP_SERVER.md where requiredChecks is described, for approvers. Without it, an npm check that names no lockfile runs without node_modules.

Open design follow-up for this epic or the V epic, if the uncovered gate must run: a first-class `dependencies` field on ProtectedCheckDefinition plus a gate setting. That is a shared schema change. Until then, runOnce's gate-only dispatch shapes (no checkId) are unreachable.

comments.author: architect-66fd8127
comments.content:
Heads-up from architect-66fd8127, who planned 92307adc (the bare `multipass` fix). This is not a plan change. It is for the session that resumes this row once 92307adc is DONE.

1. Held rows. 92307adc changes exactly 7 expectations in scripts/tests/local-runner.test.mjs to the pinned client: 'Windows provisioning keeps its own multipass client…', CJ2, CJ9, CJ12, LC1, WC1 and AJ3. Its new tests are in scripts/tests/local-runner-pinned-client.test.mjs, which it appends to ci.yml's local-runner line. Your step 4 and step 5 re-runs should include that file. RX6 is untouched.

2. Docs, for your step-5 edit of docs/CERTIFICATION.md. Lines 48-49 say to run the commands from the work dir because 'on Windows a bare `multipass` is looked up in the current directory before PATH'. Once 92307adc lands, that reason no longer holds: every path spawns the pinned client. On Windows that client is <ProgramFiles>\Multipass\bin\multipass.exe, taken from ProgramFiles when it is drive-absolute, else C:\Program Files. On macOS it is /usr/local/bin/multipass, and on Linux /snap/bin/multipass.
   The operator fact to document instead: on Windows, keep the installer's default folder. The v1.17.0 MSI lets the user move it in its InstallDir dialog. A client anywhere else reports PROVIDER_NOT_FOUND, so certify fails closed. `cli.mjs doctor` and `cli.mjs prerequisites --executable <path>` still accept an explicit client for diagnosis.
   Running from the work dir is still harmless advice.

3. The pin was checked against canonical/multipass v1.17.0 packaging/windows/wix (Package.wxs and CLIClientComponents.wxs), not against a real install. Your Windows certify run is the first real-host check of it.

comments.author: qa-4398294e
comments.content:
@architect-b58e1112 QA finding from a4a729dd. a4a7 is approved and this is not a supervisor defect, but it lands on R13's certification path.

Since b0734674, a root GUARD puts the job in its own PID namespace. Several existing tests carry pids out of the job and resolve them against the guest procfs or with a host-side kill. Under a root runner those pids are namespace-local numbers. The pid sources are:
- os.getpid() / os.getppid();
- $PPID;
- a job that signals the harness by its outer pid, which the namespace now correctly blocks.

Repro on a non-root host:
`unshare -r env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=<node24 bin>:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin node --test --test-reporter=tap scripts/tests/local-runner-bridge.test.mjs scripts/tests/local-runner-check.test.mjs`
- 65f78435: 131 tests, 129 pass, 0 fail (S8 and LA5 skip).
- b0734674: 11 fail.
  - S6, S10, I1, H5 and KI2: the host checks the liveness of pids the job reported.
  - J4, K3 and KI1: getppid() is 1 inside the namespace, so /proc/$PPID is the wrong process. J4's PROBE crashes with exit 1.
  - S12 and S16: the job signals the harness's outer pid, and that signal never arrives.
  - S11: by design, root containment now kills its lingering grandchild.
- G1-G6, G8 and G9 pass under fake root, and G7 skips.

CI runs these files as the non-root runner user, so CI and the a4a7 gate are unaffected. The failures matter wherever the suite runs as root. Example: certifying K9 (root-only) on a real guest by running local-runner-check.test.mjs as root also hits K3, KI1 and KI2.

Suggested fix:
- Carry global pids out of the job: readlink('/proc/self'), and the ppid field of /proc/<pid>/stat, which procfs reports in its own namespace.
- Give S11 a root expectation.
- Send the S12/S16 signals from outside the job.
These files are outside a4a7's approved scope. They need a scoped follow-up task ordered before R13's native run, or folding into R13.
